userStories.title: Implement read-only gold-DB open path
userStories.description: As a developer, I need an openGoldDb() function that applies four independent read-only guards and throws at startup if PRAGMA query_only is not 1, so the 54 GB gold DB cannot be mutated by the API/UI/cache.
acceptanceCriteria: File ~/signal-console/packages/db/src/open.ts exists
Exports function openGoldDb(path: string) using better-sqlite3
Implementation passes URI 'file:${path}?mode=ro' AND options { readonly: true, fileMustExist: true } to the Database constructor
Implementation runs PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000 and PRAGMA query_only = ON, then reads PRAGMA query_only back; throws Error('gold DB connection is not query_only') if the returned value is not 1
Default GOLD_DB_PATH constant points to a path matching ~/signal-console/data/signal-console.sqlite (NOT ~/nba-predict/data/...)
Grep across the repo shows zero occurrences of the string 'nba-predict/data/signal-console.sqlite' outside the allow-listed docs
Unit test asserts that INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and CREATE TEMP VIEW statements against the returned handle each throw an error
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
Running 'pnpm verify:no-stale-plan' exits 0
userStories.notes: better-sqlite3 does not enable `file:` URI parsing by default; the PRD §11.1 example code is incomplete. open.ts sets `process.env.SQLITE_USE_URI = '1'` at module load to make guard #1 (the `?mode=ro` URI) actually effective. The native addon loads lazily on first `new Database()` call and calls `sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_URI, 1)` once based on this env var. Guard #2 (`readonly: true`) is independent of this and continues to enforce SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY. Future db-package modules (US-005+) that import better-sqlite3 must import this module first or replicate the env-var setting before their own `new Database()` calls, since `std::call_once` makes the URI config a one-shot per process.

userStories.title: Implement detector cache DB schema and reset script
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the writable detector-cache DB schema applied and a pnpm cache:reset script so detector outputs can be persisted without touching the gold DB.
acceptanceCriteria: File ~/signal-console/packages/db/src/cache-migrations/0001-init.sql exists and creates detector_runs (id PK, detector_id, detector_version, params_hash, params_json, source_db_path, source_watermark_hash, scope CHECK IN ('game','window'), game_id, window_start, window_end, computed_at, compute_ms, UNIQUE constraint) and detector_observations (id PK, run_id FK ON DELETE CASCADE, game_id, bucket_start, bucket_end, fired, intensity, baseline_median, baseline_mad, detail_json) plus indexes idx_detector_obs_run_game and idx_detector_obs_fired
File ~/signal-console/packages/db/src/cache-migrations/runner.ts exists and is idempotent (re-running adds no rows, raises no error)
Default cache DB path is ~/signal-console/data/detector-cache.sqlite
File ~/signal-console/scripts/cache-reset.ts exists
package.json defines 'cache:reset' script that deletes detector-cache.sqlite and re-runs migrations
Unit test against an in-memory better-sqlite3 instance asserts the schema, both indexes, and the UNIQUE constraint exist after running the migration
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Migration uses CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS so runMigrations is naturally idempotent. The UNIQUE constraint test row sets game_id AND window_start AND window_end (despite scope='window') because SQLite treats NULLs as distinct under UNIQUE — without filling every key column the duplicate would be allowed. cache:reset removes the .sqlite + -wal + -shm trio, mkdir -p's data/, then openCacheDb() recreates the schema. runner.ts also sets process.env.SQLITE_USE_URI = '1' (mirroring open.ts) so module-load ordering between cache and gold-DB consumers cannot disable URI parsing process-wide.
